messages.subject: Adjusting the error threshold for calc_errorlod
messages.subject_clean: Adjusting the error threshold for calc_errorlod
messages.body_plain:
Hi,

I am in the process of cleaning some DO data and was just wondering whether there is a way that I can alter the genotyping error LOD score threshold (defaults to 2) in calc_errorlod()?

Thanks in advance,

Harry

messages.subject: Re: [Rqtl2-disc] Adjusting the error threshold for calc_errorlod
messages.subject_clean: [Rqtl2-disc] Adjusting the error threshold for calc_errorlod
messages.body_plain:
I don’t understand what you mean. There is no threshold used by calc_errorlod(). The results are dependent on the error_prob argument in calc_genoprob(), but I think not dramatically so.

karl

messages.body_plain:
calc_errorlod() gives you a set of error LOD scores. You can use whatever threshold you want for defining which genotypes might be errors.

karl

messages.subject: MAGIC design
messages.body_plain: Hi I have three different recipient parents crossed with one donor parent separately. I have ~100 RILs from each of these three crosses. Can I use R/qtl2 for this design? what should be the cross design?
messages.body_snippet: Hi I have three different recipient parents crossed with one donor parent separately. I have ~100 RILs from each of these three crosses. Can I use R/qtl2 for this design? what should be the cross desi

messages.subject: Re: [Rqtl2-disc] MAGIC design
messages.body_plain:
I would view this as a NAM population, rather than MAGIC. They would need to be treated as three separate two-way RIL, with cross type "riself". R/qtl2 doesn't currently have the functionality for a combined analysis of three crosses.

karl
